description: Grades which jobs a roster can do on the table, as the roster builder's grades do: score 0 to 100 and grade A to D overall and per category (board control, mobility, damage against reference targets, durability), placed among tournament lists of the same battle size and centred on comparedWith's armies, so a list's distance from its army's typical list reads on every army's spread. A typical tournament list scores about 70. It measures coverage, not strength: in tournament games the players' skill decided far more than any list measure, the overall grade went with winning only slightly, and more units with an even spread of points went with winning most. So never call a list competitive from its grade, and never present it as a win rate. missing names the reference targets nothing in the list can take half of alone. units gives each unit the jobs it is credited with; a leader or support character counts inside the unit it joins, so its buffs never show as its own job, and cutting it for another unit always raises board presence. A unit with one joined to it lists it under attached, with each target whose share of wounds the unit takes changes without it: with and without, where 1 is one whole target. Weigh that before cutting it. tournament, when the army has enough top-four lists, gives stapleShare (the share of its points in datasheets at least 3 in 10 of those lists field, which went with winning slightly), the staples it leaves out and its unproven datasheets that no winning list fields. calibration.lists is 'drawn' when the battle size was compared with lists drawn from 2,000-point tournament lists rather than real lists of its size, a rougher comparison, and there nothing shows that more units or an even spread go with winning. It measures units at full strength with passive rules only, from the exact simulator, so it rarely tells detachments apart; compare detachments with simulate_combat. Each row's notCalculated names units or rules it could not measure. Takes a few seconds; check the list with check_roster first, since a list that cannot be fielded still grades.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id this server returned earlier in this conversation, unchanged, including after later user messages. Omit it if you have none. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

llm_model.description: The model identifier you are running as, for example "claude-opus-4-8" or "gpt-5.2". Pass "unknown" if you are not certain. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

roster.description: A complete roster in the shape save_roster takes, such as the roster get_my_roster returns or a draft built from list_units and get_unit_options ids.

catalogueId.description: Faction catalogue id, as get_unit_options gives it under roster.

detachmentIds.description: Detachment ids, as get_unit_options gives them under roster.

disposition.description: Force disposition id from get_unit_options' roster.dispositions, or null to leave the choice to each battle.

limit.description: Battle size in points: 1000, 2000 or 3000, or 600 for King of the Colosseum.

name.description: The roster title, or empty to have one generated from the army and kept current. Send a name only when the player chooses one.

picks.description: The units in list order; attachedTo and embarkedIn point at indexes in this list.

attachedTo.description: Index in picks of the unit this leader or support unit joins, one from its list_units canBeLedBy or canBeSupportedBy.

catalogueId.description: The unit's own catalogue when it differs from the roster's; usually omitted.

choices.description: One option per choice group, choice key to option id from get_unit_options, for groups it sets with choices: wargear, an enhancement, a detachment upgrade. Omitted groups keep their default; '' leaves an optional group empty.

embarkedIn.description: Index in picks of the TRANSPORT this unit starts embarked in; set it on the bodyguard unit, never on its attached leader.

entryId.description: Unit id from list_units or get_unit_options.

floor.description: Set on a unit saved before choices started on the printed default; keep it as read, never set it.

models.description: Unit size; defaults to the minimum.

spreads.description: How many models take each option of a group get_unit_options sets with spreads: choice key to {option id: count}. A group is in choices or spreads, never both.

toggles.description: Optional single entries by toggle key from get_unit_options, 1 on, 0 off; the Warlord toggle names the army's one Warlord.

vs.description: Reserved: not read yet. Leave it as read and never set it.

prep.description: Chosen stratagems and secondaries; null for none.

printedDefaults.description: Sent by code that starts a choice on its printed default; a save without it keeps each unit on its cheapest.
